text:
William Nylander has 21 points in 17 games, 10 of them goals, and Toronto is mostly talking about something else. This week's headlines are about his coach, with Yahoo Sports carrying Jim Hiller's line about "Spending Less Time In The Neutral Zone Waiting For The Puck." Our numbers back the complaint more than you'd guess from the scoresheet.

At five on five the Leafs take 43.5% of the shot attempts with Nylander on the ice and 40.7% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), well below their level without him. He's shooting 20% on 6.8 expected goals, and Toronto has scored 7.8 more goals than its chances deserved with him out there. Evolving-Hockey saw the same shape last season: real offense against 97th-percentile competition, with a defensive cost in the bottom 6% of forwards.

None of that makes him a fake. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 9.5 primary shot assists per 60, and 60% of his shots came off the rush. Our range still projects 84 to 115 points. Watch whether the even-strength share climbs before the shooting cools.
headline: Nylander's points are loud. His five-on-five isn't.
